profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility MAD1, at Calle de Albasanz 71, Madrid, 28037, Spain. Digital Realty's own property listing confirms this address as MAD1, but this session's fetch did not return a confirmed square footage figure for it specifically.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC; outside the United States, the company's international footprint spans Europe, including Spain, alongside Asia-Pacific and Latin America. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Madrid metro footprint, concentrated along Calle de Albasanz and Calle de Emilio Muñoz in the city's eastern Julian Camarillo/Barajas data center corridor, coded MAD1 through MAD4 on the company's own metro listing. Digital Realty markets its Madrid properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand as part of its European interconnection and colocation footprint, alongside other European metros not tracked in this US-weighted registry.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K reports its international portfolio, including its European metros, by region and country rather than by individual building specifics, a disclosure pattern consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, not unique to this entry.

Spain's data center sector has grown substantially in recent years, with Madrid and Barcelona as the country's two primary hubs; industry and trade coverage has repeatedly named Digital Realty among the largest colocation operators active in the Madrid market alongside competitors also expanding their own Spanish footprints.

profile.regional_context: Madrid is one of Spain's primary data center and interconnection hubs, with Digital Realty's cluster concentrated in the Julian Camarillo and Barajas districts in eastern Madrid. Naturgy and Iberdrola are among the principal Spanish electric utilities serving Madrid-area commercial and industrial customers, including data centers.
